papers.title: Cartilage Tissue Engineering by the 3D Bioprinting of iPS Cells in a Nanocellulose/Alginate Bioink
papers.abstract: Cartilage lesions can progress into secondary osteoarthritis and cause severe clinical problems in numerous patients. As a prospective treatment of such lesions, human-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) were shown to be 3D bioprinted into cartilage mimics using a nanofibrillated cellulose (NFC) composite bioink when co-printed with irradiated human chondrocytes. Two bioinks were investigated: NFC with alginate (NFC/A) or hyaluronic acid (NFC/HA). Low proliferation and phenotypic changes away from pluripotency were seen in the case of NFC/HA. However, in the case of the 3D-bioprinted NFC/A (60/40, dry weight % ratio) constructs, pluripotency was initially maintained, and after five weeks, hyaline-like cartilaginous tissue with collagen type II expression and lacking tumorigenic Oct4 expression was observed in 3D -bioprinted NFC/A (60/40, dry weight % relation) constructs. Moreover, a marked increase in cell number within the cartilaginous tissue was detected by 2-photon fluorescence microscopy, indicating the importance of high cell densities in the pursuit of achieving good survival after printing. We conclude that NFC/A bioink is suitable for bioprinting iPSCs to support cartilage production in co-cultures with irradiated chondrocytes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及任何人工智能方法，与AI驱动生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML integration into any bioprinting workflow stage; purely experimental cell printing and material characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用iPS细胞3D生物打印构建软骨移植物。
summary_zh.method: 将iPS细胞与辐照软骨细胞共打印于纳米纤维素/海藻酸盐生物墨水。
summary_zh.result: NFC/A生物墨水支持iPS细胞增殖并形成透明样软骨组织。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞培养和组织染色验证软骨形成。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a cartilage tissue construct using 3D bioprinted iPS cells as a treatment for cartilage lesions.
summary_en.method: Co-printing iPS cells with irradiated chondrocytes in a nanofibrillated cellulose/alginate bioink.
summary_en.result: The NFC/A bioink supported cell proliferation and formation of hyaline-like cartilage with collagen type II expression.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture and histological staining confirmed cartilage formation.
